facts: Select future Stellantis vehicles are expected to integrate Mobileye REM cloud-enhanced ADAS beginning in 2027.
Mobileye states REM covers more than 95% of public roads in the United States and Europe.
Five of the world's ten largest automakers contribute data to REM; Mobileye reports more than 8 million contributing vehicles and 34 billion miles during the prior year.

Mobileye raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 revenue guidance by 2%, to a $1.935-$2.015 billion range.
The Mentee acquisition closed in early February and reduced cash by $591 million net of cash acquired; the quarter also included a $3.788 billion non-cash goodwill impairment.
The board authorized up to $250 million of share repurchases, intended partly to offset dilution from stock compensation and Mentee acquisition shares.
Mobileye scheduled investor events for August 12, September 8 and September 29, 2026, including Evercore's ADAS, AV & AI Forum on September 29.
The issuer states more than 250 million vehicles worldwide have been built with Mobileye EyeQ technology to date.
The issuer reiterates that Intel retains majority ownership following Mobileye's independent listing.
On September 3, 2026, Mobileye's board designated Chief Operating Officer Yaacov Kobi Ohayon as the company's principal operating officer and as an executive officer for Section 16 purposes.
Ohayon has served as COO of the Mobileye organization since 2020 and has been employed by the company and subsidiaries since 2017; the filing says his responsibilities expanded over time.

The board stated that the designation recognizes the scope of Ohayon's existing responsibilities and does not change his duties, responsibilities, employment status or existing compensation arrangements.
Mobileye's current investor-relations events page lists the Evercore 9th Annual ADAS, AV & AI Forum for September 29, 2026 at 9:40 AM EDT and provides a webcast link.

Mobileye announced scheduled participation in Evercore's 9th Annual ADAS, AV & AI Forum on September 29, 2026.
The company said it plans to webcast fireside chats when possible and direct investors to its Events & Presentations page for exact timing and access.
The announcement explicitly states that event participation and dates are subject to change.
Mobileye disclosed that on September 3, 2026, Executive Vice President Business Development & Strategy Nimrod Nehushtan transitioned to a part-time role focused on corporate strategy.
Mobileye disclosed that Vice President of Business Development Nimrod Brickman will continue to lead the company's business development activities following the transition.
As of the September 10 filing, Nehushtan's existing compensation arrangements had not been modified in connection with the role transition.
Mobileye's current Investor Relations events page lists Evercore's 9th Annual ADAS, AV & AI Forum for September 29, 2026 at 9:40 AM EDT.

The event remains an information-update window; the issuer page does not promise a product, financial or commercial announcement.
Founder Prof. Amnon Shashua informed Mobileye's board that he intends to step down as CEO upon appointment of a successor after 27 years leading the company.
The board said it will hire an executive search firm and conduct a comprehensive CEO search; Shashua remains a director and has been offered the Chairman role after a new CEO is appointed.
The issuer said the transition is intended to preserve continuity of leadership, strategy and execution while positioning the company for its next growth phase.
Mobileye stated that Intel beneficially owns approximately 77% of the company, preserving a controlling-shareholder governance consideration during succession.

Operating cash flow was $210 million in the first half of 2026 versus $322 million a year earlier; property-and-equipment purchases were $51 million versus $28 million, while cash paid for Mentee Robotics net of cash acquired was $591 million.
Mobileye states cash generated by operations is its primary liquidity source and that it expects 2026 capital expenditures to be higher than 2025 as it invests in next-generation product development.

Mobileye disclosed a manufacturing relationship with STMicroelectronics for EyeQ and an agreement with TSMC to manufacture imaging-radar components and some future EyeQ generations as part of an effort to establish redundancy and better control its supply chain.
